claim: “Yā Sīn is the heart of the Qur'an — whoever recites it, Allah writes for him the reward of reciting the Qur'an ten times.”
detail: Al-Albānī grades this narration mawḍūʿ (fabricated). Bashār ʿAwwād Maʿrūf and Zubair Ali Zai both grade it ḍaʿīf (weak). At-Tirmidhī himself calls it gharīb and notes its chain is known only through a single route.
note: Sūrat Yā Sīn is of course part of the Qur'an and reciting it is good. What is not established is this specific claim about its reward.

claim: “Recite Sūrat Yā Sīn over your dying.”
detail: Graded ḍaʿīf by all four graders recorded for this narration: al-Albānī, Muḥammad Muḥyī al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, Shuʿayb al-Arnaʾūṭ and Zubair Ali Zai.
note: Scholars have differed on acting on this. It is widely practised, but it does not rest on an authenticated chain, so we do not present it here as established.
